newsitem.title: JAPAN: JDB, banks to give loan for Tokyo land development.
newsitem.headline: JDB, banks to give loan for Tokyo land development.

text.p: Japan Development Bank (JDB) and a syndicate involving three foreign banks will provide financing to a consortium that will develop land in central Tokyo once owned by the defunct Japanese National Railways, bank officials said on Monday.

An official at JDB said it had agreed to provide financing for up to 40 percent of the total construction cost to the consortium, comprising Singapore's Alderney Investments, Matsushita Electric Works Ltd and Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd.

JDB said it had provided a loan at a fixed rate of 2.8 percent to be paid annually for 25 years. The purpose of the loan is to build office buildings on the land, which the consortium successfully bid for in February.
The official declined to disclose the amount of the loan.

The rest of the financing, about 53.3 billion yen, will be raised through a syndicate set up by HSBC Markets, the finance arm of the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank Corp, and Citibank, a HSBC Markets official in Tokyo said.
The loan has been underwritten by the two banks and Banque Nationale de Paris. The group has not disclosed the terms, but the HSBC official said that they were "extremely attractive".
